note: Hebrew/Aramaic Bible (Westminster Leningrad Codex): the designated Hebrew original. It is not the Vorlage of every version (the LXX and the Peshitta sometimes read another Hebrew text), but it is the only Hebrew in the corpus.
SBL Greek New Testament: the designated Greek original of the New Testament.
PTA's Greek Bible also holds the New Testament: another edition of the Greek original, so not a translation.
PTA Septuagint, the designated Greek Old Testament: translated from Hebrew (a Vorlage that sometimes differs from the Masoretic text).
Judges in Codex Vaticanus (Rahlfs's B text), the other Greek text of Judges.
Theodotion's Daniel: a Greek translation of Hebrew/Aramaic Daniel with the Greek additions (Prayer of Azariah, Song of the Three).
2 Esdras (Esdras B) translates Hebrew Ezra-Nehemiah, which OSHB holds as two works; naming either would join a container to one of its parts (patristica/versions.py).
Greek translation of a lost (or, for Sirach, only partly surviving) Hebrew or Aramaic original that is not in the corpus: the Greek is the original here.
Composed in Greek.
Greek additions to Daniel (Old Greek and Theodotion); a Semitic original is debated and not extant.
The Odes: a Greek collection of biblical and other canticles.
Rahlfs's Septuagint: a second edition of the Greek Old Testament, translated from Hebrew.
Greek translation of a lost (for Sirach, partly surviving) Semitic original not in the corpus: the Greek is the original here.
Composed in Greek.
Jerome's Vulgate Old Testament, translated from Hebrew (iuxta Hebraeos).
The Vulgate Psalter is the Gallicanum: Jerome's revision of the Old Latin against the Hexaplaric Greek, not his Psalter iuxta Hebraeos.
Jerome translated Esther from Hebrew; the Greek additions follow as 10.4-16.24, from the Greek (secondary source: pta-lxx/esth).
Jerome translated Daniel from Hebrew/Aramaic; 3.24-90 and chapters 13-14 come from Theodotion's Greek (secondary source: pta-lxx/danthdt).
Old Latin, translated from Greek; Jerome left these books unrevised. Baruch 6 is the Letter of Jeremiah (pta-lxx/epjer).
Jerome translated Tobit and Judith from an Aramaic text that is not in the corpus.
Vulgate New Testament: the Old Latin revised against the Greek (Jerome for the Gospels).
Peshitta Old Testament, translated from Hebrew, with LXX influence in places (secondary source: pta-lxx).
Peshitta Sirach was translated from Hebrew, which is not in the corpus.
Translated from Greek. Baruch and the Psalms of Solomon have been argued to come from Hebrew; the Greek is the usual view.
Syriac Tobit follows the short Greek recension (GI, pta-lxx/tobvatal) to 7.11 and a text close to GIII after it.
3 Esdras is Greek 1 Esdras (Esdras A), translated from the Greek.
Translated from Theodotion's Greek Susanna.
Translated from Theodotion's Greek Bel and the Dragon.
Translated from a lost Greek text (2 Baruch and its Letter, 4 Ezra), not in the corpus.
The Prayer of Manasseh came into Syriac through the Didascalia; its Greek is in the Odes (pta-lxx/odes), a collection, not the same work.
A Syriac collection of canticles drawn from the Peshitta books themselves, not a translation of the Greek Odes as a work.
Peshitta New Testament, translated from Greek (2 Peter, 2-3 John, Jude and Revelation from the later Syriac versions, also from Greek).
Sahidic Old Testament, translated from the Septuagint.
Sahidic Daniel follows Theodotion's Greek.
Sahidic Tobit follows the short Greek recension (GI).
Sahidic New Testament, translated from Greek.
Zohrab's Armenian Old Testament: the revised translation from the Septuagint (the first, Syriac-based translation is not what survives).
Armenian Daniel follows Theodotion's Greek.
Armenian Tobit: from Greek, close to the short recension (GI) with readings of the long one (pta-lxx/tobsin).
Greek 1 Esdras (Esdras A) under another book code.
Translated from Greek 2 Esdras, which the corpus has only as one work for both books (pta-lxx/ezraneh).
Armenian New Testament, revised from the Greek in the 5th century after a first translation from Syriac.
Ge'ez Old Testament, translated from the Septuagint (later revisions from Arabic and Hebrew are not recorded).
Greek 1 Esdras (Esdras A) under another book code.
Ge'ez Tobit follows the short Greek recension (GI).
Translated from Greek 2 Esdras, which the corpus has only as one work for Ezra and Nehemiah (pta-lxx/ezraneh).
4 Ezra (Ezra Sutuel) 12-14 (#217), translated from a lost Greek text; the Syriac 4 Esdras (pta-peshitta/4esr) is a sister translation, in its version group by the book code.
Ge'ez 1 Enoch, translated from Greek (an Aramaic original survives only at Qumran); the Greek covers chapters 1-32 and fragments (another edition: first1k/tlg1463/tlg001/1st1K-grc2).
Translated from a Greek text that is lost (Jubilees) or not in the corpus (4 Baruch, Paralipomena Jeremiou).
Ethiopic works translated or adapted from Arabic (Ethiopic Clement, Sinodos, Synaxarion) or of uncertain source (Teaching of Mysteries); the source is not in the corpus.
Composed in Ge'ez.
Wulfila's Gothic New Testament, translated from Greek.
Gothic fragments of Nehemiah, translated from Greek 2 Esdras, which the corpus has only as one work for Ezra and Nehemiah (pta-lxx/ezraneh).
King James Version: Old Testament from Hebrew (the Bomberg Rabbinic Bible).
King James Version: New Testament from Greek (the Textus Receptus; SBLGNT stands for the Greek).
American Standard Version: Old Testament from Hebrew.
American Standard Version: New Testament from Greek (Westcott-Hort).
World English Bible: Old Testament from Hebrew.
World English Bible: New Testament from Greek (Majority Text).
